10.1002_adfm.75616: Lithium‐sulfur batteries (LSBs) have been considered as one of the most promising next‐generation energy storage systems, however, they suffer from poor conductivity of sulfur, shuttling effects of polysulfides, and sluggish reaction kinetics. In this work, a cascade anchoring strategy was employed to synthesize a Fe‐N/P co‐doped porous carbon catalyst (Fe‐N/P‐PC) with high single‐atom Fe loading (9.0 wt.%). The strategy combines spatial confinement, glucose‐assisted chelation and pyrolysis to form stable Fe‐(N/P) 4 ‐C sites within a hierarchical porous structure. The resulting S@Fe‐N/P‐PC as cathode for LSBs delivers high capacities of 1263.5 mAh g −1 at 0.2 C and 530.0 mAh g −1 at 8 C, and maintains 701.4 mAh g −1 after 1000 cycles at 1 C. Under high sulfur loading of 6.8 mg cm −2 and lean electrolyte of 5.9 µL mg −1 , it achieves a high areal capacity of 5.38 mAh cm −2 with 87.8% initial capacity retention after 200 cycles at 0.1 C. A 52.1 mg sulfur pouch cell exhibits a high initial energy density of 410.6 Wh kg −1 and 83.3% retention after 350 cycles, demonstrating its high practical potential.
10.1002_adfm.76495: Aqueous Zn–Mn batteries represent a promising technology for grid‐scale energy storage, yet their practical deployment is hindered by interfacial instability at both electrodes, including dendrite growth, hydrogen evolution reactions (HER), and corrosion at the anode and irreversible dissolution at the cathode. Herein, hypotaurine (HypTau) is introduced as a multifunctional electrolyte additive to achieve synergistic interfacial regulation on both sides, supported by comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) calculations and experimental analyses. On the Zn anode, HypTau preferentially adsorbs on the Zn surface, forming a water‐repellent electric double layer and an in situ‐constructed gradient organic–inorganic hybrid solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), while also serving as an effective pH buffer. These three components collectively suppress water‐induced side reactions, homogenize Zn 2 + flux, and lower the nucleation overpotential, enabling uniform Zn deposition. On the MnO 2 cathode, HypTau adsorption induces electron accumulation at the interface, thereby establishing a negatively charged environment which in turn facilitates Mn 2 + enrichment and promotes its re‐deposition during charging, thus significantly improving the reversibility of the two‐electron reaction. As a result, Zn||Zn symmetric cells achieve an extended cycling lifespan of 2155 h, and Zn||MnO 2 full cells without pre‐added Mn 2 + retain stable operation for over 5000 cycles.
10.1002_adma.202502865: Interfacial localized charges and interfacial losses from incompatible underlayers are critical factors limiting the efficiency improvement and market‐integration of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Herein, a novel interfacial chemical tuning strategy is proposed involving proton transfer between the amine head of pyridoxamine (PM) and the phosphonic acid anchoring group of [4‐(3,6‐dimethyl‐9H‐carbazol‐9‐yl)butyl]phosphonic acid (Me‐4PACz), with simultaneous enhancement of charge delocalization through electrostatic attraction between opposite charged molecules. The Me‐4PACz‐PM charge polarization interface modulates the nickel oxide (NiO x ) charge states and the coordination environment at buried interfaces, consequently enhancing p‐type conductivity and obtaining a more compatible band arrangement. The high‐coverage and wettability of the NiO x /Me‐4PACz‐PM underlayer also facilitate the deposition of high‐quality perovskite films, releasing lattice strain and mitigating trap‐assisted non‐radiative recombination. Attributing to the implementation of charge polarization tunable interfaces, small‐area devices and modules with an aperture area of 69 cm 2 achieved impressive power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 26.34% (certified 25.48%) and 21.94% (certified 20.50%), respectively, and unencapsulated devices maintained their initial PCEs ≈90% after aging for 2000 h (ISOS‐L‐1) and 1500 h (ISOS‐D‐1). The broad applicability of charge polarization tunable interfaces and the successful scaling of large‐area modules provide a reference for expanding PSCs applications.
10.1002_aenm.202504922: Zinc metal powder (ZnMP) anodes present significant advantages over conventional zinc foil anodes in aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs), offering higher electrochemically active surface area and improved mass utilization. However, the 3D morphology of ZnMP particles poses challenges for crystallographic control, as their random orientations and large surface areas intensify hydrogen evolution reactions (HER), corrosion, and dendritic growth. Here, a dual‐functional etching strategy using trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) is reported to selectively modify ZnMP surfaces and enrich thermodynamically stable (002) crystal planes. Upon dissociation, TFA releases H + ions that preferentially etch high‐energy facets, while CF 3 COO − anions selectively adsorb onto (002) planes, forming protective layers that stabilize the etching process. This treatment produces a distinctive stepped hexagonal morphology enriched in (002) planes that mitigates parasitic reactions and promotes uniform zinc deposition. The TFA‐modified ZnMP (TFA@ZnMP) electrodes exhibit remarkable stability, operating for over 1000 h in symmetric cells. In practical 4 × 3 cm 2 pouch cells paired with V 2 O 5 cathodes, the electrodes retain 79.8% of their capacity after 1000 cycles at 10 A g −1 . Density functional theory calculations and phase‐field modeling confirm the preferential ion adsorption mechanism and its contribution to enhanced electrochemical performance. These findings establish this surface‐engineering strategy as a scalable pathway for high‐performance AZIBs.
10.1002_anie.2561729: High-energy-density lithium metal batteries (LMBs) require electrolytes that can simultaneously support stable lithium metal anodes and high-voltage cathodes such as NMC811 operated up to 4.5 V. Here, a molecular engineering strategy is introduced in which a carbonyl group and a trifluoromethyl group are incorporated into a glycol-ether-type backbone to produce a fluorinated alkoxyethyl acetate solvent, 2-(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)ethyl acetate (TFE-EA), used as the main solvent in LiFSI-TFE-EA-FEC electrolytes. This design breaks the symmetric bidentate solvation typical of ether solvents, establishes carbonyl-dominant solvation, and depresses the solvating ability and oxidation reactivity of the ethereal oxygen, as revealed by combined DFT, NMR, FTIR, Raman, and AIMD analyses. The resulting TFE-EA-based electrolyte exhibits enhanced oxidative stability, improved lithium plating/stripping efficiency, dense and uniform lithium deposition, and robust cathode-electrolyte interphases in Li||NMC811 cells cycled to 4.5 V, delivering markedly superior capacity retention and Coulombic efficiency compared with ethereal counterparts. Parallel studies on the non-fluorinated alkoxyethyl acetate MEA and its ether analog EME confirm that ester introduction alone improves oxidative stability and cycling, while fluorination further amplifies these benefits. This work establishes alkoxyethyl acetates, exemplified by TFE-EA, as a promising solvent platform for practical, high-voltage LMB electrolytes.
10.1016_j.cej.2025.166556: Biomass-derived carbon-based electrocatalysts often suffer from low performance in hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) at high current density, limiting their industrial use. Herein, a Mn 2 Mo 3 O 8 -Ni heterojunction is integrated into a self-supported lignin-derived carbon framework on nickel foam (LC-Mn 2 Mo 3 O 8 @Ni/NF) to enhance HER performance. Electrochemical tests demonstrate that LC-Mn 2 Mo 3 O 8 @Ni/NF exhibits effective HER activity under pH-universal conditions (Alkali: E − 10/ − 2000 = −54.7/322.9 mV; Acidic: E − 10/ − 2000 = −39.5/431.5 mV; Neutral: E − 10/ − 600 = −84.2/421.9 mV). Density functional theory calculations reveal that the synergy of lignin-derived carbon and the heterojunction redistributes electrons, creating an electron-rich carbon layer and electron-deficient Mn 2 Mo 3 O 8 @Ni, increasing active sites. The optimized d -band center enhances *H adsorption/desorption (ΔG ⁎H = −0.12 eV) and lowers the water dissociation energy (0.61 eV), facilitating the Volmer step and boosting HER activity across all pH conditions. Furthermore, LC-Mn 2 Mo 3 O 8 @Ni/NF maintains stability at −500 mA cm −2 for 140 h without significant performance loss, attributed to its super-hydrophilic, gas-repellent properties, and corrosion-resistant porous self-supported lignin-derived carbon, thus facilitating HER across pH-universal conditions. This research provides an efficient catalyst for HER and offers valuable insight for developing high-performance biomass-derived carbon-based electrocatalysts for water electrolysis.
10.1038_s41467-026-75485-9: Practical electrochemical energy conversion requires electrocatalysts that coordinate multiple elementary steps at spatially distinct active sites, yet atomic-level control of such site-specific reactivity within a single heterogeneous particle remains challenging. Here we propose and realize atomic-scale gradient strain as a design concept for heterogeneous electrocatalysis. Using Pd@Pt core-shell tetrahedra as a model system, we construct a continuous lattice-strain gradient across individual 3–4 atomic-layer Pt {111} epitaxial shells, where lattice-mismatch-driven compression relaxes from edges to center regions. This single-particle strain gradient, spanning approximately −8% to −2%, spatially links *O2 activation at highly compressed sites with *OH weakening at moderately compressed sites through kinetically accessible intermediate redistribution. The catalysts exhibit competitive oxygen reduction reaction performance, with mass and specific activities of 2.19 A mgPt⁻1 and 3.01 mA cm⁻2 at 0.9 V vs reversible hydrogen electrode, while retaining 91% activity after 20 k cycles. In membrane electrode assemblies, they achieve 0.57 A mgPt⁻1, and peak power densities of 2.10 W cm⁻2 in H2 − O2 and 1.16 W cm⁻2 in H2−air, with over 90% performance retention after 20 k cycles. Strain engineering tunes catalyst reactivity, but single strain cannot optimize all steps in oxygen reduction concurrently. Here, the authors report strain gradients within individual Pd@Pt core-shell tetrahedra that link distinct local reaction sites, improving fuel-cell activity and durability.
10.1039_d5ta04638f: An ultra-thin Co-MOF based heterostructure with well-defined geometries is constructed successfully. This heterostructure effectively regulates interfacial charge states, accelerates charge transfer, and enhances the electrochemical performance.
10.1109_tte.2025.3540409: A fusion of local and global feature-based explainable diagnosis methods is proposed for lithium-ion battery (LIB) degradation modes in this article. The method captures fault features from the discharge curves of a semi-battery model. Voltage curves are transformed into incremental capacity (IC) curves, converted into 2-D images and subjected to feature extraction to obtain high-dimensional features. A battery fault feature-extraction module based on a local-global feature fusion module is designed to enhance feature saliency by extracting long-term dependency information. To explain the learning process, a battery fault explainability determination module is designed to analyze the attention points of the proposed method on the overall IC curve image changes by highlighting the focus areas. The explainability analysis of the decision-making process was accomplished by integrating the IC curve analysis, including variations in the IC peaks, to establish a physical correlation. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method were verified through experiments.
10.1109_tte.2025.3546924: Economic consideration and service life have constrained the development of fuel cell vehicles (FCVs). Moreover, due to the complexity of operating conditions, the energy management strategy (EMS) must adapt to various unknown scenarios. This article proposes a novel health-aware real-time multiobjective (HR-MO) EMS based on vehicle-cloud architecture for medium and heavy-duty multigear FCV. Specifically, a robust energy source degradation model is incorporated into the multiobjective EMS. The vehicle speed prediction model trained on multisource data is finely designed based on bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) to achieve high accuracy, lightweight, and strong adaptability. The self-adjusting dynamic programming (DP) algorithm is employed as a solver to enhance computational efficiency and energy efficiency. Finally, in order to meet instantaneous power demand, a vehicle-cloud collaborative EMS is designed to optimize the output power of the fuel cell (FC) in the cloud and adaptively adjust the battery power in the vehicle. Simulation results show that the proposed strategy under different unknown scenarios can reduce hydrogen fuel consumption, the high-power/idle operation time of the FC, the number of start/stop cycles, and the variation in FC load. Furthermore, an experiment test is conducted for real-time performance verification.
